key_insight: Alzheimer’s and psychiatric polygenic risk showed distinct diagnostic associations in young-onset presentations, with no detected associations with measured plasma biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk may offer information distinct from plasma biomarkers, but added diagnostic value remains unproven.
method: Studied 687 European-ancestry participants: 195 healthy controls, 283 with primary psychiatric disorders, 55 with Alzheimer’s disease and 154 with other neurodegenerative diseases.
Computed five polygenic risk scores excluding APOE; adjusted models for age, sex and APOE ε4 dose.
Assessed plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 in 332 participants.
evidence_signal: Alzheimer’s genetic risk was associated with Alzheimer’s disease (OR 1.69 per SD, 95% CI 1.17–2.45); adding it to NfL did not improve psychiatric-versus-other-neurodegenerative discrimination meaningfully (AUC 0.764 versus 0.773).
watch_item: European-only ancestry and a small Alzheimer’s subgroup limit generalizability; diagnostic utility needs larger, longitudinal validation.
paper_title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
